extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and natural philosophers (readers of Newton's Principia; 17th-century scholars) / students of classical mechanics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and foundational axioms (laws) of motion from Newton's Principia (Latin): precise definitions of absolute/relative time, space, place, and motion; laws I–III (inertia, change of motion proportional to impressed force, action/reaction); corollaries and experimental guidance (pendulums, projectiles, composition/resolution of forces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempus absolutum (absolute time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tempus absolutum, mathematicum, vera atque pura, fluxus est uniformis, et natura sua sine relatione ad externum quidvis; duratio rerum quaeque est eadem sive motus celeres sive tardi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish true (absolute) time from sensible/relative measures; absolute time cannot be altered by changes in motions, and its duration is invariant even if apparent motions accelerate or retard. Astronomical 'equation of common time' and experiments (oscillatory clocks, eclipses of Jupiter's satellites) supply evidence/corrections to sensible measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempus relativum / vulgare (relative/common time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relativum (vulgare) tempus est mensura motus sensibilium et externorum, ut hora, dies, mensis, annus — sensibiles mensurae, quarum inaequalitates astronomi corrigunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common time is practical for daily use but differs from absolute time; one must correct relative time (e.g., unequal natural days) via astronomical equations to recover true measurements for philosophical/mathematical purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatium absolutum (absolute space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spatium absolutum, natura sua sine relatione ad externum quodvis, semper manet similare & immobile: est locus immotilis primarius ad quem translationes veri motus referri possunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat absolute space as the unmoving reference whose parts maintain mutual positions 'ab infinito in infinitum'; use it conceptually to define true motion (motus verus) even though its parts are not directly perceptible by the senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatium relativum (relative space)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relativum est spatii mensura seu dimensio quaelibet mobilis, quae a sensibus nostris per situm suum ad corpora definitur, & a vulgo pro spatio immobiIis usurpatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative space is the sensible measure (position with respect to bodies) used in practice, e.g., 'dimension of submarine, aerial, or celestial space defined by relation to the earth.' Remember relative and absolute spaces may coincide in species and magnitude but differ numerically when bodies move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus (place)
rubrics_metrics.description: Locus est pars spatii quam corpus occupat, estque pro ratione spatii vel absolutus vel relativus; pars spatii, non situs corporis vel superficies ambiens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define place as the part of space a body occupies (primary). Distinguish place from mere situs/position or surrounding surface; equal solids have equal loci though surfaces may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motus absolutus vs motus relativus (absolute vs relative motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motus absolutus est translatio corporis de loco absoluto in locum absolutum; relativus de relativo in relativum. Quies relativa est permansio in regione navigii; quies vera est permansio in parte spatii illius immoti.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples (ship, sailor, earth) to distinguish motions observed relative to a moving frame from true motion with respect to absolute space. Decompose combined motions into contributions from true motions of frames and relative motions within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties distinguishing true and relative motion (proprietates, causae, effectus)
rubrics_metrics.description: True motion and relative motion differ by properties, causes, and effects: true rest/motion implies mutual rest/motion of bodies; true motion is generated/changed only by forces impressed on the moving body, whereas relative motion can change without forces on that body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To identify true motion, inspect causes (forces impressed directly on body) and effects (e.g., centrifugal tendencies). Relative motions can arise purely from motion of reference bodies; thus experiments aiming to detect true motion should seek effects not attributable to mere relative translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal test for true motion (forces impressed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motus verus nec generatur nec mutatur nisi per vires in ipsum corpus motum impressas; motus relativus generari & mutari potest sine viribus impressis in hoc corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect true motion by checking whether forces are impressed on the body. If changes in motion occur without forces on that body but due to motion of other bodies, the motion is relative. Use tension, centrifugal effect, and force measurements to infer true motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect test for absolute circular motion (centrifugal tendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectus: in motu circulari relative sola vires recedendi ab axe nullae sunt; in vero & absoluto majores vel minores pro quantitate motus. Conatus recedendi ab axe (e.g., water rising to sides of rotating vessel) indicates true circular motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experiments (rotating vessel with water, motion of suspended buckets) to observe centrifugal tendencies: if fluid climbs the sides, a true circular motion is present. Such effects cannot be explained by mere relative translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex I (Law I: Inertia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus omne perseverare in statu suo quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum, unless impressed forces change that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principle of inertia: bodies persist in uniform rectilinear motion or rest unless acted upon. Examples provided: projectiles continue in their motions unless retarded by air resistance and pulled downward by gravity; wheels (trochus) continue rotating unless resisted by air. Use this as fundamental premise in mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex II (Law II: change of motion proportional to impressed force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutationem motus proportionalem esse vi motrici impressae, & fieri secundum lineam rectam qua vis illa imprimitur. Doubling the force doubles the change, etc.; vector composition applies (additive in direction of impressed force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes of motion (momentum/quantity of motion) are proportional to the impressed force and occur along its line of action. Composition of forces follows parallelogram rule; when forces act simultaneously or successively, changes add vectorially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lex III (Law III: action and reaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actioni contrariam semper & aequalem esse reactio: actiones corporum in se mutuo sunt semper aequales & in partes contrarias dirigi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Examples: finger pressed by a stone experiences equal pressure back; horse pulling stone via rope experiences equal opposite pull. Mutations induced are equal in the bodies acted upon (in terms of changes of motion), leading to conservation-related corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium I (resultant via parallelogram of forces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus viribus conjunctis diagonalem parallelogrammi eodem tempore describere, quo latera separatis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two forces M and N act simultaneously, the body moves as if acted on by the diagonal of the parallelogram formed by those forces. This justifies parallelogram rule for composition of simultaneous forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium II (composition and resolution of forces; mechanical examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositio & resolutio virium: any direct force AD can be resolved into oblique components AB & BD and vice versa; mechanical demonstrations via wheels, radii, pulleys, levers show how weights and radii relate to effective turning forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric/mechanical constructions (radii, perpendiculars, similar triangles) to compute resolved components that do work (e.g., trahendo radium perpendiculariter yields effective torque). Applies widely to machines (wheels, tympans, levers, pulleys, cunei).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium III (conservation of quantity of motion / momentum invariant under internal actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitas motus, quae colligitur capiendo summam motuum factorum ad eandem partem, & differentiam factorum ad contrarias, non mutatur ab actione corporum inter se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutual interactions between bodies (action + reaction) do not change the total quantity of motion (sum/difference of parts toward same/opposite directions). Use this to predict post-collision motions by preserving total 'motus' (momentum) and applying decomposition into components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium IV (center of gravity behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commune gravitatis centrum corporum duo vel plurium, ab actionibus corporum inter se, non mutat statum suum vel motus vel quietis; commune centrum vel quiescit vel movetur uniformiter in directum (absent external forces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal forces cannot change the motion/state of the system's center of gravity. The motion of a system can be characterized by motion of its center of gravity; use this for system-level analyses and simplifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium V (equivalence of motions in uniformly moving enclosed spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporum dato spatio inclusorum iidem sunt motus inter se, sive spatium illud quiescat, sive moveatur idem uniformiter in directum, sine motu circulari.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments inside a uniformly moving ship yield same relative motions as if ship were at rest — statement of Galilean relativity for inertial frames. Use to argue that uniform translation of whole system has no detectable internal mechanical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollarium VI (equal accelerative forces in parallel lines leave relative motions unchanged)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora moveantur quomodocunque inter se, & a viribus acceleratricibus aequalibus secundum lineas parallelas urgeantur; pergem omnia eodem modo moveri inter se, ac si viribus illis non essent incitata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If equal accelerative forces act in parallel on all bodies, relative motions among them are unchanged — another expression of relativity: uniform acceleration of the entire system does not alter internal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium: applications and experimental methods (projectiles, pendulums, corrections for air resistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using laws I–II, deduce projectile parabola, free-fall in duplicate ratio of times, pendulum timing, and correct experimental observations (pendulum oscillation amplitudes, velocities) for air resistance to approximate vacuum behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: correct measured motions (e.g., pendulum amplitudes, velocities before/after reflection) by geometric chord methods to infer vacuum-equivalent motions; use long pendula, large separations, and careful subtraction of air resistance effects to validate laws and measure true motions. Employ experiments (suspended spheres, threads, tensions) to infer true circular motions, magnitudes of motion, and verify action-reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for inferring true motion from tensions and differences of apparent motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Argumenta desumi possunt partim ex motibus apparentibus (differences) & partim ex viribus quae sunt motuum verorum causae & effectus — e.g., two spheres connected by a string revolving about a common center: tension reveals conatus recedendi ab axe and hence true circular motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurable quantities like string tension, filament forces, and differential tensions under alternating applied forces to compute quantities and determinations of true motion (including in otherwise 'vacuo' thought experiments with distant fixed stars as reference).
